summary: Tesla, Inc. (TSLA, NASDAQ Global Select) designs, manufactures and sells electric vehicles, related software and services, and energy generation and storage products. Robotaxi and Optimus remain pre-commercial options. SELL is warranted in this Valuatum equity research report dated 18 August 2026, with a 12-month target price of 276.00 USD against a current price of 328.58 USD, implying -16.0% downside. Market capitalisation is USD 1,297.7 bn and enterprise value is USD 1,296 bn. The central concern is not the existence of growth opportunities but the scale and timing required to support the quoted valuation.

The valuation tension is concentrated in two pre-revenue options. Robotaxi / Autonomous Mobility Network carries EV of USD 807,837m, or 62.3% of group EV, while Optimus / Humanoid Robotics carries EV of USD 353,003m, or 27.2%; together they hold 89.6% of EV despite contributing approximately 0.0% of FY2025A reported revenue. Automotive and Energy generate revenue of USD 82,056m and USD 12,771m respectively, but receive only 6.5% and 3.9% of EV. The stock trades at 178.8x 2026E P/E and 104.7x 2026E EV/EBITDA, while the 2028E peer median EV/EBITDA is 8.5x.

The target price uses a 2029E EV/EBIT sum-of-the-parts, selecting 12x for Automotive, 25x for Energy, 25x for Robotaxi and 25x for Optimus, with 100% weight on the SOTP and 0% on the USD 40.8 / sh ROE/P/BV indication. Discounted division values produce a target price of 276.0 USD. The scenario bridge gives 49.06 USD / sh and -85.1% downside in Bear, 490.81 USD / sh and +49.4% upside in Base, and 753.70 USD / sh and +129.4% upside in Bull. These are boundary cases, not probability-weighted inputs.

thesis.title: Robotaxi Scale
thesis.text: Robotaxi must expand from tens to low hundreds of unsupervised vehicles to approximately 3.0 million by 2029, generating revenue of USD 90.0bn and EBIT of USD 31.5bn. Waymo already operates over 3,000 vehicles and serves 500,000 paid rides weekly, making Tesla’s required ramp the decisive execution risk behind a 62.3% EV allocation.

thesis.title: Optimus Volume Ramp
thesis.text: Optimus valuation requires approximately 3.3 million units sold annually by 2029 at an average selling price near USD 30,000, producing revenue of USD 99.0bn and EBIT of USD 14.9bn. That volume is roughly six times the 542,000 industrial robots installed globally in 2024, while Tesla remains at internal pilots and installing Gen 3 lines.

thesis.title: Automotive Margin
thesis.text: Automotive EBIT margin has fallen from 16.8% in 2022 to 4.6% in 2025, despite FY2025A revenue of USD 82,056m and gross profit of USD 13,292m. The 2029 case assumes core EBIT of USD 7,200m valued at 12x, leaving group value dependent on option businesses rather than durable car-business profitability.

thesisBreaker: An unsupervised robotaxi fleet that remains legally or operationally small through 2028 would eliminate the 62% EV allocation to Robotaxi and drive valuation towards the bear case.

valuePools.name: Robotaxi / Autonomous Mobility Network
valuePools.economics: Revenue USD 0m (0.0%) · Gross profit USD 0m (0.0%) · EBIT USD 0m (0.0%, modelled allocation) · EV USD 807,837m
valuePools.text: Robotaxi is an emerging option rather than a reported operating segment: current revenue and gross profit are both USD 0m, yet the allocation assigns it EV of USD 807,837m, or 62.3% of group EV. The instructed 2029 case requires revenue of USD 90.0bn, EBIT of USD 31.5bn and a 35% EBIT margin from approximately 3.0 million unsupervised vehicles. At USD 30,000 of annual revenue per vehicle, the fare economics require USD 0.375–0.60 per occupied mile. The arithmetic is internally consistent, but reaching the fleet would require roughly a 10,000-fold increase from today’s unsupervised count. Waymo has over 3,000 vehicles and 500,000 paid rides weekly, while Tesla remains in the tens to low hundreds. California provides testing only, with a CPUC driverless paid-deployment permit still required.

valuePools.name: Optimus / Humanoid Robotics
valuePools.economics: Revenue USD 0m (0.0%) · Gross profit USD 0m (0.0%) · EBIT USD 0m (0.0%, modelled allocation) · EV USD 353,003m
valuePools.text: Optimus is an emerging option with current revenue and gross profit of USD 0m, but it receives EV of USD 353,003m, or 27.2% of group EV. The instructed 2029 case requires approximately 3.3 million units, revenue of USD 99.0bn and EBIT of USD 14.9bn at a 15% margin and an average selling price near USD 30,000. The required volume is about six times the 542,000 industrial robots installed globally in 2024 and roughly 13 times Goldman’s 2030 base-case shipment pool. Fremont has design capacity of 1 million units a year, while Giga Texas targets 10 million, but neither represents demonstrated output. Agility’s Digit is already working commercial shifts at nine facilities and Figure has 40 units at BMW, leaving reliability, cost and third-party demand unproven.

valuePools.name: Automotive
valuePools.economics: Revenue USD 82,056m (86.5%) · Gross profit USD 13,292m (77.8%) · EV USD 84,760m
valuePools.text: Automotive is Tesla’s principal current profit engine, generating FY2025A revenue of USD 82,056m and gross profit of USD 13,292m, but its EV allocation is only USD 84,760m, or 6.5% of group EV. The model treats the division as mature, with 2029 sales near USD 84,000m and core EBIT of USD 7,200m valued at 12x. That allocation is supported by current sales but not by current EBIT quality: group EBIT was only USD 4,355m in 2025, while Automotive EBIT margin fell from 16.8% in 2022 to 4.6%. Tesla delivered 1.64 million vehicles in 2025, down nearly 9%, versus BYD’s more than 2.25 million BEVs. BYD pricing pressure, fading US credits and shared production capacity make margin recovery plausible but demanding.

valuePools.name: Energy Generation & Storage
valuePools.economics: Revenue USD 12,771m (13.5%) · Gross profit USD 3,802m (22.2%) · EV USD 50,364m
valuePools.text: Energy Generation & Storage is the higher-quality current business, producing FY2025A revenue of USD 12,771m and gross profit of USD 3,802m, with EV of USD 50,364m, or 3.9% of group EV. Deployments reached 46.7–46.9 GWh in 2025 and Q2 2026 deployments of 13.5 GWh were up 53% sequentially, although reported gross margin declined and one source cited a USD 240m warranty charge. The instructed 2029 case models sales of USD 13,100m and applies 25x to core EBIT of USD 2,100m, making the multiple dependent on limited forecast growth. CATL, Fluence and BYD remain competitors, while Shanghai Megapack trial production targets 40 GWh and Houston targets up to 50 GWh. Cell availability remains a constraint shared with Automotive.

reverseValuation.intro: The scenario bridge tests how Robotaxi and Optimus execution changes Tesla’s enterprise value, with unsupervised robotaxi fleet size in 2028–2029 as the primary swing factor. Revenue scales linearly with vehicles once fares and utilisation are fixed, while Optimus provides the second-largest sensitivity. The Bear case removes the instructed option EBIT and values the cash businesses at a manufacturer multiple; the Base case retains the instructed scale; the Bull case adds higher margins or a multiple above 30x. These are operating boundary cases, not probability-weighted target inputs.

coreAnalysis.heading: How the company creates economic value
coreAnalysis.text: Tesla currently earns money through Automotive and Energy Generation & Storage. Automotive generated FY2025A revenue of USD 82,056m and gross profit of USD 13,292m, while Energy generated revenue of USD 12,771m and gross profit of USD 3,802m. Group EBIT was USD 4,355m, a 4.6% margin, down from a 16.8% margin in 2022. Robotaxi and Optimus are not reported segments, and any revenue they generate is included in Automotive and was commercially immaterial in FY2025A. Nevertheless, Robotaxi is allocated EV of USD 807,837m and Optimus USD 353,003m. Together they represent 89.6% of group EV while contributing approximately 0.0% of reported FY2025A revenue. The instructed 2029 case adds revenue of USD 90,000m and EBIT of USD 31,500m from Robotaxi, plus revenue of USD 99,000m and EBIT of USD 14,900m from Optimus. Core Automotive and Energy sales remain broadly flat to modestly higher. The economic value therefore rests on converting manufacturing, software and data advantages into two businesses that have not yet demonstrated commercial output. Waymo’s 3,000-plus vehicles and Baidu’s 3.2 million fully driverless rides in Q1 2026 provide stronger observed autonomous scale, while Optimus remains at internal pilots. This evidence supports SELL.

coreAnalysis.heading: Putting the divisions back together
coreAnalysis.text: The cross-division bridge makes the valuation dependence measurable. Instructed 2029 sales of USD 285,676m are USD 191,000m above 2025, with Robotaxi and Optimus supplying USD 189,000m of the increase. Group EBIT reaches USD 55,658m, USD 51,000m above 2025, and the two options contribute USD 46,400m. Current businesses support a 2026–2027 run-rate of roughly USD 94,000m–USD 100,000m of sales and USD 7,000m–USD 8,000m of EBIT, but consensus EBIT for 2028 is only USD 9,900m versus USD 17,713m in this model. Applying 15x to 2026E EBIT of USD 6,904m supports approximately USD 104,000m of EV, only 8% of the USD 1,296,000m control total. Applying 15x to 2029E EBIT of USD 55,658m supports approximately USD 835,000m, still below current EV. The selected 25x option multiples therefore carry the valuation. The bridge also requires gross capex to rise from USD 8,591m in 2027 to USD 26,030m in 2028 and USD 75,400m in 2029, while free cash flow to firm moves from positive USD 4,711m to negative USD 3,240m and then negative USD 14,500m. Net cash falls from USD 12,347m in 2026E to USD 3,400m in 2029E. SELL follows because future execution must arrive before cash generation does.

coreAnalysis.heading: Scenarios and verdict
coreAnalysis.text: The Bear outcome of 49.06 USD per share and -85.1% downside requires a regulatory stop, a safety event or a 2027 fleet still measured in hundreds, leaving the cash businesses valued as a manufacturer and the option EBIT removed. The Base outcome of 490.81 USD per share and +49.4% requires multi-city paid unsupervised Robotaxi operations by 2027, manufacturing capacity in the hundreds of thousands by 2028, and meaningful third-party Optimus shipments in 2027–2028. The Bull outcome of 753.70 USD per share and +129.4% requires those volumes plus higher margins or a market willing to pay more than 30x. The earliest indicators are a California CPUC driverless paid-deployment permit, third-party fleet counts above the low thousands, Optimus shipments and ASP disclosure, and FY2028 group EBIT above USD 9,900m consensus. More geofenced territory without more vehicles would not prove the Base case. The central debate is whether Tesla can turn a vertically integrated vehicle and vision-only platform into a 3.0 million-vehicle Robotaxi network before regulatory, competitive and capital constraints intervene, or whether the USD 1,296,000m EV is capitalising two pre-revenue programmes ahead of evidence. The balance of evidence favours SELL.

risks: Unsupervised approval delay (Automotive): NHTSA action or a California permit block could prevent the fleet expanding beyond hundreds, with NHTSA action and CPUC permit status as the early warning - HIGH impact and a thesis-breaker if it occurs.

AV competition splits the fare pool (Robotaxi / Autonomous Mobility Network): Waymo, Apollo Go and Uber partnerships could fragment the USD 400,000m addressable market and make USD 90,000m of revenue unreachable, with competitor city expansions as the early warning - HIGH impact and structural.

Humanoid reliability and cost miss (Optimus / Humanoid Robotics): failure to reach a USD 25,500 cost or reliable household performance would destroy the 15.0% EBIT thesis, with internal test failures and high warranty as the early warning - HIGH impact and structural.

Cell and capex collision (Optimus / Humanoid Robotics): simultaneous factory scale-ups could exhaust the balance sheet as 2029 free cash flow to firm reaches negative USD 14,500m, with delayed Texas Giga timelines as the early warning - MEDIUM impact and manageable.

Vehicle price war and fading EV credits (Automotive): BYD pricing and lost incentives could trap core Automotive EBIT at a 4.6% margin, with sequential MSRP cuts as the early warning - MEDIUM impact and structural.
catalysts: California CPUC driverless paid-deployment permit (near-term, Robotaxi / Autonomous Mobility Network): approval would unlock the largest US fare pool and distinguish a Texas-and-Florida pilot from national deployment.

TCMV / EU FSD recognition vote (near-term, Robotaxi / Autonomous Mobility Network): the October 2026 committee outcome could unlock EU supervised scale, although it would not by itself prove Robotaxi EBIT.
Optimus third-party shipments and ASP disclosure (medium-term, Optimus / Humanoid Robotics): volume targeted by summer 2027 would convert design capacity into demonstrated real selling prices.
Group EBIT exceeding USD 9,900m consensus (long-term, Automotive): FY2028 earnings above consensus would validate option EBIT scaling in reported results.

Capex trajectory against free cash flow to firm (long-term, Robotaxi / Autonomous Mobility Network): a USD 75,000m capex print alongside negative USD 14,500m free cash flow to firm would test the balance sheet against the volume ramp.

faqs.q: Is Tesla, Inc. a buy in 2026?
faqs.a: No. Tesla is rated SELL with a 12-month target price of 276.00 USD against a current price of 328.58 USD, implying -16.0% downside. Robotaxi and Optimus represent 89.6% of EV despite approximately USD 0m of reported FY2025A revenue, while the stock trades at 178.8x 2026E P/E and 104.7x 2026E EV/EBITDA. The valuation requires approximately 3.0 million robotaxis and 3.3 million Optimus units annually by 2029.

Tesla’s 12-month fundamental target price is 276.00 USD, compared with the current price of 328.58 USD and implied downside of -16.0%. The target is derived from a 2029E EV/EBIT sum-of-the-parts using 12x for Automotive, 25x for Energy, 25x for Robotaxi and 25x for Optimus. The SOTP carries 100% weight; the ROE/P/BV indication of 40.8 USD / sh carries 0% weight.

Tesla is rated SELL because USD 1,296 bn of EV depends primarily on two pre-revenue options. Robotaxi carries EV of USD 807,837m and requires revenue of USD 90,000m, EBIT of USD 31,500m and approximately 3.0 million unsupervised vehicles by 2029. Optimus carries EV of USD 353,003m and requires revenue of USD 99,000m and EBIT of USD 14,900m. Current deployment and production evidence remain far below those requirements.

The valuation is demanding relative to current earnings and peer benchmarks. Tesla trades at 104.7x 2026E EV/EBITDA and 178.8x 2026E P/E, versus a 2028E peer median EV/EBITDA of 8.5x. The control EV also represents 20.1x revised 2029E EBITDA. The valuation can be supported only if Robotaxi and Optimus reach their instructed 2029 volumes and retain selected option multiples of 25x.

faqs.q: What is Tesla’s bear and bull case?
faqs.a: The Bear case values Tesla at 49.06 USD / sh, or -85.1%, after a regulatory stop, safety event or 2027 fleet still measured in hundreds removes the instructed option EBIT. The Base case is 490.81 USD / sh, or +49.4%, and requires the instructed scale. The Bull case is 753.70 USD / sh, or +129.4%, requiring those volumes plus higher margins or a market willing to pay above 30x.

sources: Primary data: Valuatum Equity Research, Tesla, Inc. report dated 18 August 2026 (the value-map allocations, anchor market capitalisation of USD 1,297.7 bn, enterprise value of USD 1,296 bn and share price of 328.58 USD). The 2029 estimates use an instructed execution scenario and should not be mistaken for company guidance or a base-case assumption.

Competitor context: Waymo operates over 3,000 autonomous vehicles and serves 500,000 paid rides weekly; Baidu reported 3.2 million fully driverless rides in Q1 2026; Agility’s Digit works commercial shifts at nine customer facilities; Goldman’s 2030 base-case humanoid shipment pool is 250,000 units. Waymo’s fully burdened cost estimates are reported as a USD 2.50–45.00 per-mile range, so the datapoint is unusually broad and should not be treated as a clean unit-cost benchmark.

Market data: TSLA at 328.58 USD as of 18 August 2026; FY2025A revenue of USD 94,827m, comparable EBIT of USD 4,355m and EBITDA of USD 10,503m; 2026E EBIT of USD 6,904m and EBITDA of USD 12,383m; revised 2029E EBIT of USD 55,658m and EBITDA of USD 64,556m behind the target bridge. Share-price history and market profile are attributed to Financial Modeling Prep.
